names.legendary: Saguaro, the Thorned Saint of Drought

lore.common: Has been ignored for six months and considers this the ideal relationship.
lore.uncommon: Offers a hug to anyone who calls it adorable. They do not call it adorable twice.
lore.rare: Fires warning needles at anyone approaching with a watering can. It has won every gardening argument.
lore.epic: Grew an army of spiny arms overnight and transformed the town's coat shop into an accidental acupuncture clinic.
lore.legendary: Stands watch in a desert where no rain has fallen for a thousand years. Saguaro knows where the last drop is hidden and refuses to tell the clouds.

names.legendary: Recyclora, Judge of the Second Life

lore.common: Rejects one perfectly ordinary yoghurt pot because it still smells of strawberries.
lore.uncommon: Shakes its glass bottles through the quiet street like an exhausted maraca.
lore.rare: Sorts an entire household's rubbish overnight, including Dad's suspicious collection of broken cables.
lore.epic: Dragged every incorrectly sorted bin into the town square for a public hearing. The residents pleaded guilty to pizza boxes.
lore.legendary: Sorted a whole town's rubbish in one night, then put the town hall in the paper bin because it was mostly forms.

names.legendary: Cratalia, Maestro of the Bottle Symphony

lore.common: Rattles across the pavement sounding like a badly tuned marching band.
lore.uncommon: Stacks empty bottles so high that the first breeze conducts them.
lore.rare: Plays a different note on each bottle whenever the collection lorry approaches.
lore.epic: Rolled into the town festival and turned a thousand empty bottles into a thunderous glass orchestra. Even the brass band surrendered.
lore.legendary: Cratalia rescued every broken glass instrument from the old opera house and rebuilt its music in a crate of shimmering bottles. The melodies ring whenever rain touches the glass.

names.legendary: Floralis, Keeper of the First Spring

lore.common: Waits for someone to admire it before producing one spectacular sneeze.
lore.uncommon: Attracts every bee in the garden and insists they are a private orchestra.
lore.rare: Changes colour to match the nearest visitor. Wedding photographers are losing their minds.
lore.epic: Bloomed in the centre of the football pitch and grew so magnificent that the referee banned tackling anywhere near it. The final score was three bouquets to one.
lore.legendary: Floralis sheltered the first bee beneath its petals when the world was still cold. Every spring the flowers wake to retell the story in colour.

names.legendary: Summitella, House at the World's Edge

lore.common: Arrives at camp with one pole missing and blames the mountain goats.
lore.uncommon: Flaps its flysheet all night like a ghost learning to play drums.
lore.rare: Pulls up its pegs after dark and waddles to a nicer view. Sleepers rarely appreciate the upgrade.
lore.epic: Sheltered an entire climbing party through a blizzard by expanding into a canvas fortress. The mountain now has an unofficial hotel.
lore.legendary: Summitella pitched itself on a peak no climber had reached and kept a lamp burning for every lost wanderer. They say its door always opens onto the way home.

names.legendary: Admiral Churnwell, Conqueror of Tides

lore.common: Splashes tourists on the dock and spins away before anyone can complain.
lore.uncommon: Churns the river into froth like a giant whisk stirring tea.
lore.rare: Paddles backwards when the captain turns the wrong lever. The ferry returns to the same pier in disguise.
lore.epic: Spun against a flood so fiercely that the water climbed the banks in reverse. The salmon finally had a downhill commute.
lore.legendary: Admiral Churnwell carried the last riverboat through a century's worst storm using a single turning wheel. His wake carved the safe channel that sailors follow to this day.

names.legendary: Apronarch, Shield of a Thousand Feasts

lore.common: Collects flour in its pockets and sneezes little white clouds whenever dinner is served.
lore.uncommon: Ties its strings in impossible knots when the cook is late. Calls it meal preparation.
lore.rare: Catches boiling soup splashes on its enchanted front and flicks them back into the pot. The chef now wears it into battle.
lore.epic: Whipped up a flour tornado at the grand bake-off, lifting every pie into the air. They landed perfectly sliced. The judges awarded first prize to the weather.
lore.legendary: Apronarch has protected royal kitchens through a thousand feasts and six terrible cooking shows. Its pockets hold every secret recipe ever lost to history.

names.legendary: Pinnora, Queen of the Harvest Dance

lore.common: Unties its giant bow whenever its wearer needs both hands. It claims to be a free spirit.
lore.uncommon: Blends into floral wallpaper to avoid washing the dishes. The wallpaper is beginning to smell of stew.
lore.rare: Its strings reach across the garden to pluck ripe berries into its pockets. One morning it accidentally harvested a garden gnome.
lore.epic: Spun through the village harvest dance and swept a hundred dancers into an enchanted waltz. The barn is still dancing three autumns later.
lore.legendary: Pinnora's endless pockets can hold a whole year's harvest without spilling a seed. Once, during a famine, she fed seven villages and still had room for a biscuit.

names.legendary: Bobbington, Shield of the Open Sea

lore.common: Makes its wearer look like a bright orange marshmallow with arms.
lore.uncommon: Has a whistle so shrill that every seagull on the beach answers it.
lore.rare: Floats so eagerly that its wearer rises an inch above the floor before reaching the water.
lore.epic: Inflated during a rowing lesson and lifted the entire canoe crew into the air. The instructor is still insisting this counts as a water sport.
lore.legendary: Bobbington guarded the sailors of a lost fleet through a hundred black storms. Though the ships vanished, every traveller wearing its orange crest was carried safely to shore.

names.legendary: Grand Admiral Sunseed, Lord of Wings

lore.common: Promises a feast for birds and immediately loses the entire budget to a squirrel.
lore.uncommon: Checks every pigeon's manners before admitting it. The queue has formed a union.
lore.rare: Shakes off raiding squirrels with the precision of a carnival ride. The sparrows sell tickets.
lore.epic: Spilled one enchanted seed and summoned a flock so vast the garden shed lifted off like an aircraft carrier.
lore.legendary: Birds from every kingdom answer its morning bell. Sunseed charges one sunflower seed per beak, except the robin, who somehow owns the place.

names.legendary: Nestorion, Architect of a Thousand Nests

lore.common: Built a lovely wooden home. Everyone moved into the hedge just to annoy it.
lore.uncommon: Measures visitors at the entrance. The robin keeps pretending to be a sparrow to get cheaper rent.
lore.rare: Pretends to be full of chirping birds when the cat is underneath. It has never had a tenant.
lore.epic: Added so many floors overnight that the original branch needed scaffolding. The blue tits have booked the penthouse.
lore.legendary: Nestorion builds homes for birds not yet hatched. Even the phoenix has a reservation, although fire insurance remains a difficult subject.

names.legendary: Flapjaw, Devourer of Junk Mail

lore.common: Snaps on the postman's glove every morning and pretends it is an accident.
lore.uncommon: Whistles a winter wind through the hall during the quietest scene of any film.
lore.rare: Swallows every envelope before spitting them out in reverse alphabetical order.
lore.epic: Refused to release the postman's sleeve until he read every letter aloud. By teatime the entire street knew who had bought a new dishwasher.
lore.legendary: Flapjaw once devoured a thousand years of unwanted advertisements and mailed each one back to the sender. The kingdom enjoyed silence for a century, broken only by the occasional postcard.

names.legendary: Mycelia, Queen Beneath the Fairy Ring

lore.common: Pops up on the lawn overnight as though it has sneaked in after the gates were locked.
lore.uncommon: Grows in an impossibly neat circle. Insists nobody should ask what happens in the middle.
lore.rare: Changes colour when touched and leaves a faint trail of glowing spores for curious woodland creatures.
lore.epic: Raised a ring of giant toadstools across the football pitch before a championship match. The players ended up holding a very confused fairy banquet.
lore.legendary: Mycelia's hidden threads link the roots of the ancient forest, carrying messages beneath the earth. The trees whisper secrets to her, and she has never told a single squirrel.

names.legendary: Saucerella, Collector of Forgotten Rain

lore.common: Overflows when the plant is watered, but somehow leaves the soil dry.
lore.uncommon: Hides a secret puddle beneath the pot until someone steps in it barefoot.
lore.rare: Runs a luxury hotel for slugs beneath the geranium. Breakfast is included.
lore.epic: Captured so much runoff from the greenhouse that it turned the conservatory into a miniature marsh. The frogs have applied for residency.
lore.legendary: Saucerella collected rainwater from a hundred droughts, one drop at a time. When the oldest garden began to die, it poured the whole treasure back into the roots.

names.legendary: Terra Potentia of the Lost Orchard

lore.common: Cultivates three weeds for every flower, then displays them proudly.
lore.uncommon: Refuses to be moved, even when it is clearly sitting on the garden hose.
lore.rare: Swaps the seeds of neighbouring pots overnight. The roses now grow tiny courgettes.
lore.epic: Grew a giant pumpkin so quickly that the patio lifted off its foundations. The barbecue arrived in the pond without a reservation.
lore.legendary: Terra Potentia sheltered the final seed of a lost orchard in her cracked clay belly. When the last winter passed, a hundred fruit trees rose from her soil in a single spring.

names.legendary: Rosamund, the Thorn-Crowned Sleeper

lore.common: Pricks your finger with a thorn every time you try to smell it.
lore.uncommon: Drops one petal onto every love letter to ensure it gets the credit.
lore.rare: Makes strangers fall in love with the nearest inanimate object. The gardener has proposed to his wheelbarrow twice.
lore.epic: Wrapped the palace in a single night's worth of briars. The royal gardeners now enter with sandwiches and a detailed rescue plan.
lore.legendary: Rosamund sleeps inside a rose that blooms only when someone keeps an impossible promise. Kings have offered gold; one stubborn child brought back a lost library book.

names.legendary: Borealis, Chariot of the Impossible Turn

lore.common: Goes downhill louder than its passengers can scream. Takes this as encouragement.
lore.uncommon: Races through icy corners so tightly that everyone's cheeks arrive separately.
lore.rare: Crossed the finish line before its crew finished climbing in. The judges awarded the medal to the empty seat.
lore.epic: Cut a racing line through a frozen waterfall and emerged on the mountain's far side. The timing officials asked whether teleportation was permitted.
lore.legendary: Borealis once raced the northern lights along a glacier. Its runners still carve glowing tracks that no morning sun can melt.

names.legendary: Fenrusk, Rider of the Northern Lights

lore.common: Cannot start until every dog agrees on the direction. They never agree.
lore.uncommon: Swerves toward every passing squirrel, even in a snowstorm.
lore.rare: Leaves a trail of glowing pawprints across frozen lakes. The wolves follow it like a map.
lore.epic: Outran the blizzard so completely that winter arrived late to an entire village. The sled dogs demanded overtime sausages.
lore.legendary: Fenrusk once carried the lost aurora across the polar night, each husky pulling a different color. The sky still glows in their footprints.

names.legendary: Skaterion, Rider of the Storm Road

lore.common: Starts moving the moment somebody says hold my drink.
lore.uncommon: Runs out of charge precisely at the bottom of the steepest hill.
lore.rare: Can glide up a vertical wall for three seconds, which is enough to frighten every pigeon on it.
lore.epic: Chased a thunderstorm across the city to recharge, outrunning the rain and leaving a glowing trail of skateboard sparks.
lore.legendary: Skaterion rode a ribbon of lightning from the mountains to the sea. Every storm now leaves one brief shining road across the sky for those brave enough to follow.

names.legendary: Skyskid, the Roof-Riding Rebel

lore.common: Throws its rider into a flailing dance the moment they try to look cool.
lore.uncommon: Spins in place whenever someone leans forward. It claims that counts as travelling.
lore.rare: Slides sideways through doorways without scratching the frame, but steals every slipper along the way.
lore.epic: Whirled through an entire furniture showroom, rearranging the sofas into a racetrack. The customers started taking bets.
lore.legendary: Skyskid rode a ribbon of static electricity above the rooftops at dawn. It still parks on the chimney and charges rent to the pigeons.

names.legendary: Wakeripper, the Wave-Crowned Racer

lore.common: Soaks the one beachgoer who has just changed into dry clothes.
lore.uncommon: Roars past the quietest cove, then pretends the seagulls started it.
lore.rare: Leaps between breaking waves as though the sea is a staircase built just for it.
lore.epic: Jumped a wave, landed on the pier and rolled into the ice-cream queue without slowing down. The cashier offered it a napkin.
lore.legendary: Wakeripper chased the great storm across seven seas and stole a crest of white foam from every wave. Its wake still shines silver under moonlight.

names.legendary: Slalombra, the Blade of the Mountain

lore.common: Crosses its twin at the worst possible moment and sends the skier into a snowdrift.
lore.uncommon: Catches the chairlift gate with its tip and demands another trip uphill.
lore.rare: Carves a perfectly curved path through deep powder without disturbing a single falling snowflake.
lore.epic: Raced down the face of a glacier and drew a giant spiral visible from the valley. The mountain guides now sell postcards of the track.
lore.legendary: Slalombra was carved from winter's first falling icicle. She can ski along the narrow crest of a snowflake, leaving behind a trail of blue light that never melts.

names.legendary: Sledwyn, the Sled That Outran Spring

lore.common: Steers directly into a soft snowbank and pretends it was the plan all along.
lore.uncommon: Hates going uphill so much that it tries to drag its owner back down with it.
lore.rare: Slides over dry grass and cobblestones as smoothly as fresh snow, leaving bewildered wheel tracks behind.
lore.epic: Shot down the mountain and across the village square, bringing a snowstorm of cheering children into the bakery.
lore.legendary: Sledwyn carried the last snowflake of winter across a sunlit valley to keep a child's promise of one final ride. The hill still turns white for a heartbeat whenever it passes.

names.legendary: Ollivern, Lord of the Upside-Down Peak

lore.common: Attaches itself upside down and sends its rider sliding backwards toward the ski instructor.
lore.uncommon: Loosens one binding at exactly the moment a photograph is taken.
lore.rare: Rides a half-pipe without touching it, carving glowing crescents through the powder below.
lore.epic: Spun above the resort for an entire night, whipping the snowfall into a colossal funnel shaped like a snowboarder's helmet.
lore.legendary: Ollivern rode the underside of an avalanche as though it were a wave. The mountain now turns upside down whenever it hears applause.

names.legendary: Neridon, Rider of the First Wave

lore.common: Throws its rider off just before the camera clicks.
lore.uncommon: Collects sand in its wax like other monsters collect trophies.
lore.rare: Hears distant swells in its sleep and begins inching toward the beach before dawn.
lore.epic: Rode a storm surge straight through a beachfront hotel, leaving a perfect trail of sea foam down the grand staircase.
lore.legendary: Neridon rode the first wave before the oceans had shores. When the sea is perfectly still, the old board is said to be listening for its return.

names.legendary: Somnimbus, Captain of the Sleeping Isles

lore.common: Deflates one tiny breath at a time. It likes its victims to wake up wondering why the floor is so close.
lore.uncommon: Squeaks like a rubber duck whenever somebody rolls over. It considers this a bedtime song.
lore.rare: Bounces sleeping campers across the tent when it dreams. One woke up in the wrong sleeping bag and apologised.
lore.epic: Inflated so fiercely that an entire campsite floated above the clouds. The campers gave it five stars for the view.
lore.legendary: Carries whole dreaming cities across the sea on its cushion of air. At dawn it deflates, leaving confused tourists and a furious lighthouse keeper.

names.legendary: Matthazar, Warden of the Restless Wild

lore.common: Unrolls itself at three in the morning after being packed away. A terrible tentmate.
lore.uncommon: Can locate the only sharp pebble in a field and move it directly beneath your shoulder.
lore.rare: Rolls its sleeper into a sausage whenever it hears snoring. Nobody has complained from inside.
lore.epic: Snapped open inside the scout hut and cocooned twelve campers and a canoe. Everyone reported excellent sleep and disturbing dreams of rubber.
lore.legendary: Matthazar can soften mountains into beds for wandering giants. Its own owner still wakes up with a stone beneath their hip, as tradition demands.

names.legendary: Mattilda, Guardian of the Last Campsite

lore.common: Slides across the tent floor overnight so its owner wakes with their head outside the door.
lore.uncommon: Crinkles like a packet of crisps every time a camper turns over.
lore.rare: Keeps a sleeping hiker's back warm even on frozen rock, with a tiny patch of sunshine underneath.
lore.epic: Unrolled itself into a floating carpet during the storm and carried the entire camping group safely across the flooded valley. The tents followed like ducklings.
lore.legendary: Mattilda spreads a soft sleeping place wherever no bed has ever stood, from desert stone to mountain ice. Every traveller she shelters dreams of a hearth waiting somewhere ahead.

names.legendary: Aurelia, Face of the Forgotten Sun

lore.common: Drops seeds on the postman's head and pretends the wind did it.
lore.uncommon: Tracks every ray of sunlight with the intensity of a suspicious detective.
lore.rare: Turns its enormous flower face toward anyone eating sunflower seeds. There is no comfortable way to finish a snack.
lore.epic: Grew taller than the ferris wheel and turned its head so quickly that the entire fair spun with it.
lore.legendary: Aurelia held a spark of daylight in her golden petals through the longest darkness, giving the sleeping bees one morning to remember.

names.legendary: Baroness Mulchgrave, Empress of Decay

lore.common: Opens its lid exactly when the neighbours invite guests over.
lore.uncommon: Runs an underground worm apartment complex. Rent is paid in potato peel.
lore.rare: Steams so fiercely that every gardener thinks a dragon has moved in behind the shed.
lore.epic: Its fermented fumes conquered the village fete. The chemistry teacher called it innovation; the judges called an evacuation.
lore.legendary: Swallowed a royal feast's scraps and grew a palace from the leftovers. The monarch now lives in a giant pumpkin and pays rent to earthworms.

names.legendary: Binjamin, Keeper of the Second Chance

lore.common: Whacks its lid against the cupboard whenever anyone steps on the pedal too enthusiastically.
lore.uncommon: Snaps shut just as a tea bag approaches, then laughs from under the sink.
lore.rare: Refuses to swallow an important object that someone is throwing away by mistake.
lore.epic: Flung the leftovers of a birthday party into the air in one mighty lid-snap. The balloons have smelled of banana ever since.
lore.legendary: Binjamin guarded the town's discarded treasures until every missing ring, key and photograph had been returned to its owner. He still refuses to take credit, only the rubbish.

names.legendary: Discretia, Keeper of the Unspoken Duties

lore.common: Closes its lid so quietly that nobody notices the work it does.
lore.uncommon: Sits politely in the corner while the louder bathroom bins demand attention.
lore.rare: Knows exactly when to be emptied and summons the caretaker with a faint, respectful chime.
lore.epic: Organised the entire shopping centre washroom so efficiently that the mop and soap dispenser voted it head of housekeeping.
lore.legendary: Discretia has guarded the privacy of generations without revealing a single secret. Even the nosiest palace ghosts pass her corner without a whisper.

names.legendary: Aegis Amber, Keeper of Safe Hands

lore.common: Snaps its little yellow lid shut with an oddly satisfied click.
lore.uncommon: Collects abandoned needle caps and builds a surprisingly tidy nest.
lore.rare: Seals dangerous sharps inside a chamber that no curious hand can open.
lore.epic: Absorbed every stray sharp from the entire hospital in one night. The morning staff found its lid wearing a tiny gold medal.
lore.legendary: Aegis Amber stood beside the healers through the longest plague, swallowing every used needle and never opening her jaws again. Her yellow shell is kept as a symbol of safe care.

names.legendary: Binjamin, Collector of Lost Beginnings

lore.common: Waits for a thrown paper ball, then sidesteps it by one inch.
lore.uncommon: Eats crumpled drafts and burps disappointed sighs.
lore.rare: Smooths rejected ideas flat overnight, revealing the one brilliant sentence nobody noticed.
lore.epic: Swallowed every discarded proposal in the office, then regurgitated a revolutionary plan written entirely on old takeaway menus. The boss took all the credit.
lore.legendary: Collected the first drafts of a thousand failed inventions. From their crumpled pages it built one wondrous machine, whose only purpose was to give its creators a second chance.

names.legendary: Binderella, the Midnight Collector

lore.common: Falls over on bin day just as the truck turns the corner.
lore.uncommon: Flaps its lid in the wind, trying to tell the neighbours the latest gossip.
lore.rare: Rolls itself to the kerb after dark, but refuses to come back without a thank-you.
lore.epic: Led an uprising of bins through the streets one windy night. By morning every house had somebody else's rubbish and a new postcode.
lore.legendary: Took over the council's collection route when the crews were snowed in. Every bin arrived spotless, and not one wheel made a sound as it passed the sleeping houses.

names.legendary: Tulipha, the Bloom That Bought a Kingdom

lore.common: Closes its petals the moment someone prepares a camera.
lore.uncommon: Tilts its stem to eavesdrop on garden gossip and blushes in new colours.
lore.rare: Changes the colour of neighbouring flowers by whispering to their roots overnight.
lore.epic: Made every tulip in the royal gardens bloom at once, carpeting the castle in a rainbow so bright the visiting diplomats forgot their speeches.
lore.legendary: Tulipha grew from a single bulb once worth a merchant's fortune. She refused to be sold and scattered ten thousand daughter bulbs across the poor quarters, turning greed into a spring festival.

names.legendary: Verdantia, Spinner of the Summer Rain

lore.common: Aims every last jet of water at the only pair of dry shoes in the garden.
lore.uncommon: Clicks in circles while the dog tries to bite the very last droplet.
lore.rare: Waits until the family settles down for lunch, then redirects the water onto all the sandwiches.
lore.epic: Spun into a lawn-sized waterspout at the summer fair, lifting the bouncy castle into an unexpected cruise over the flowerbeds.
lore.legendary: Verdantia watered a burnt valley with a single silver turn. By dawn the hills were green and the clouds were waiting in line for their next lesson.

names.legendary: Popsyra, Ambusher of the Thirsty

lore.common: Pops up precisely beneath a lawn chair, giving its occupant a surprise fountain.
lore.uncommon: Hides beneath the grass until the mower approaches, then springs up with a metallic grin.
lore.rare: Reverses its spray in mid-air to soak the one person carrying a completely dry picnic.
lore.epic: Raised an army of buried fountains at the cricket final, launching the pitch into a choreographed water ballet.
lore.legendary: Popsyra slept under the royal gardens for a hundred droughts. When the fountains ran dry, she rose and poured an underground river into the roots of every tree.

names.legendary: Shrillcap

lore.common: Is used as a whistle by blowing across it, which makes a shriek.
lore.uncommon: Is the perfect size for a fairy's hat, according to every child.
lore.rare: Fits on any fingertip and will not come off, so its finder spends the afternoon waving like a puppet.
lore.epic: Was blown across the park in one gust and landed on every pigeon's head. The pigeons refuse to take them off.
lore.legendary: Whistled so loudly through one child's thumbs that every dog in the county came running and sat down to wait for orders.

names.legendary: Tillandra, Queen of the Empty Earth

lore.common: Lives without soil and insists dirt is a ridiculous hobby for other plants.
lore.uncommon: Drinks its weekly bath in a single gulp, then pretends it was caught in a rainstorm.
lore.rare: Floats across rooms searching for morning mist. It once followed a humidifier home and refused to leave.
lore.epic: Scattered its seeds into the sky until floating gardens bloomed above the entire city. The pigeons now have landlords.
lore.legendary: Tillandra grows from empty air and drinks the dawn itself. Her suspended gardens shade kingdoms that have forgotten what soil looks like.

names.legendary: Aloethra, Balm of the Burning Sky

lore.common: Waddles around on sticky aloe leaves. Everything it hugs comes away moisturised and faintly suspicious.
lore.uncommon: Stores healing gel in its cheeks like a hamster. Nobody has asked why it keeps a tiny bottle of suncream.
lore.rare: Its cooling slime can calm a boiling kettle in seconds. Tea enthusiasts have declared it an enemy of civilisation.
lore.epic: Turned an entire waterpark into a shimmering gel slide. Visitors entered on Tuesday and are still gently sliding toward Thursday.
lore.legendary: When the desert sun scorched an ancient kingdom, Aloethra raised a canopy of living aloe across the dunes. The people built temples beneath its leaves, then complained it was a bit damp.

names.legendary: Zhu Feng, the Unbroken Reed

lore.common: Grows three centimetres while the gardener blinks. Denies everything when confronted.
lore.uncommon: Whistles through its hollow body whenever the wind is bored, usually at 3 a.m.
lore.rare: Can grow an entire panda buffet before breakfast. The pandas have started leaving reviews.
lore.epic: Punched through a concrete car park overnight and replaced every parking space with an extremely vertical forest.
lore.legendary: Bent beneath the fiercest typhoon without breaking, then sprang upright and launched the storm's flagship back into the harbour.

names.legendary: Begonatrix, the Neverwinter Bloom

lore.common: Drops a leaf in protest whenever someone moves its pot to the other window.
lore.uncommon: Wears shiny, waxy petals and tells all the plastic flowers they're being unoriginal.
lore.rare: Grows giant listening leaves. Knows every secret spoken within two houses of its windowsill.
lore.epic: Bloomed so brilliantly pink that the entire flamingo enclosure escaped the zoo to join its garden party.
lore.legendary: The only flower that defied the first winter. Her blossoms keep their colours even beneath snow, and spring still asks her how it is done.

names.legendary: Zenboku, Keeper of the Mountain in a Pot

lore.common: Insists it is a majestic forest even though it lives beside the kettle.
lore.uncommon: Takes three hours to grow one leaf and considers this rushing.
lore.rare: Makes everyone in the room whisper. Even the washing machine switches to a gentler cycle.
lore.epic: Grew a thunderstorm over its tiny branches. The entire living room experienced mountain weather while the sofa remained in summer.
lore.legendary: Zenboku has tended a whole ancient kingdom within its ceramic bowl for centuries. Travellers need only shrink their worries to enter it.

names.legendary: Saint Crookmint, Shepherd of Winter

lore.common: Sticks to the inside of your coat pocket and smells like Christmas until August.
lore.uncommon: Can turn any cup of tea minty merely by leaning against the saucer.
lore.rare: Hooks itself to passing scarves and travels the town disguised as festive decoration.
lore.epic: Summoned a peppermint blizzard over the winter market. The snowmen smelled delicious, and the reindeer demanded hazard pay.
lore.legendary: Saint Crookmint once hooked a falling star with his striped crook and planted it atop a Christmas tree. Nobody has managed to switch those lights off.

names.legendary: Sir Walksworth, Staff of Lost Roads

lore.common: Taps its way down the pavement with the confidence of a marching band. Pigeons disagree.
lore.uncommon: Hooks every table, coat rack and shopping bag it passes. Calls them souvenirs.
lore.rare: Can sense a loose paving stone three streets away and loudly warns everyone by knocking on doors.
lore.epic: Stopped a runaway bus by hooking its bumper. The driver bowed; the owner just wanted to get to the pharmacy.
lore.legendary: Sir Walksworth remembers every footstep of those he has supported. When a lost traveller grips his handle, the stones themselves show the way home.

names.legendary: Tentaculon, the Wandering Festival

lore.common: Waits until the last peg is hammered in before deciding to fly away.
lore.uncommon: Pinches the same finger every time its folding legs are extended. It collects finger-shaped dents.
lore.rare: Stores a secret pond of rainwater above your head and drops it on the first person to say dry.
lore.epic: Folded an entire market stall into itself, including the cakes, cashier and one customer still arguing about prices.
lore.legendary: Tentaculon wanders between festivals that have not yet been announced. Entire towns wake to find a striped roof above them and a bill for venue hire.

names.legendary: Carnelia, the Flower That Outlived Kings

lore.common: Ruffles its petals whenever someone calls it a cheap flower. It has an excellent memory.
lore.uncommon: Sneaks into every wedding buttonhole and eavesdrops on the vows for gossip.
lore.rare: Lasts so long in a vase that three generations of roses have come and gone beside it.
lore.epic: Dyed an entire wedding party scarlet by releasing one furious burst of pollen. The photographer calls the pictures artistic.
lore.legendary: Carnelia blooms on the graves of forgotten promises and remembers every word spoken at a wedding. She is the reason some old couples still get mysterious flowers.

names.legendary: Hanamiya, Empress of the Last Spring

lore.common: Drops a pink petal into your tea whenever you sit beneath it. Calls this seasoning.
lore.uncommon: Blooms for four days, then demands a year's worth of compliments.
lore.rare: Releases blossoms when someone photographs it and immediately turns bare once the camera lowers. A menace to influencers.
lore.epic: Turned an entire city pink in one afternoon. Traffic wardens issued tickets to the petals; the petals paid in perfume.
lore.legendary: Hanamiya blooms only once every hundred springs, and every blossom holds a memory someone thought they'd forgotten. The most beautiful one remembers the first kiss beneath her branches.

names.legendary: Chrysanthra, Keeper of the Last Colour

lore.common: Grows so many petals that its face has become a rumour.
lore.uncommon: Blooms when all the other flowers have gone home. Insists on having the garden to itself.
lore.rare: Shoots a perfectly round pompom at anyone who calls it a daisy. Accuracy is impeccable.
lore.epic: Unfurled a flower the size of the town square, and the entire autumn festival was held inside its petals.
lore.legendary: Chrysanthra saves every colour summer forgets. When winter stole the last golden sunset, she opened one flower and painted dawn across the snow.

names.legendary: Cloveraine, Duchess of Wild Fortune

lore.common: Hides its fourth leaf the moment a child starts looking. The child has found six ants instead.
lore.uncommon: Feeds every bee in the garden and demands honey commission in return.
lore.rare: Grants tiny miracles, like finding a coin, then immediately loses the owner's keys.
lore.epic: Carpeted the championship bowling green with lucky four-leaf clovers. Every bowl struck the jack, and the referees had to invent a new sport.
lore.legendary: Lady Cloveraine wins every raffle she never enters. Legends say she stole luck from a fallen star and keeps it in one small leaf, next to a very ordinary snail.

names.legendary: Stumpurion, Keeper of the Final Over

lore.common: Falls apart the moment a nervous batter breathes too loudly.
lore.uncommon: Hides one bail in the grass at every village match.
lore.rare: Steps delicately aside as each delivery arrives, leaving the bowler questioning reality.
lore.epic: Refused to fall for an entire championship. The opposing team grew moustaches waiting for an appeal.
lore.legendary: The three sacred stumps stood through a thousand summers, and no ball could shake them. Their final defeat came from a very embarrassed pigeon.

names.legendary: Axillara, Guardian of Second Chances

lore.common: Falls over whenever you lean it against a wall.
lore.uncommon: Deliberately squeaks in quiet hallways. The entire hospital now knows its name.
lore.rare: Grants its user perfect balance during a gale, then insists on taking all the credit.
lore.epic: Crossed the entire city in one heroic leap to retrieve a forgotten birthday cake. The taxi drivers started a union.
lore.legendary: Forged from the wood of an ancient healing tree, Axillara carries weary adventurers across impossible roads. It asks only that they stop trying to use it as a coat rack.

names.legendary: Narcissara, First Voice of the Spring

lore.common: Nods so eagerly at every passing breeze that the tulips suspect sarcasm.
lore.uncommon: Trumpets the arrival of spring two weeks too early. The frost sends complaints.
lore.rare: Can persuade a stubborn snowbank to make room for a patch of flowers.
lore.epic: Blew its golden trumpet across the fields and shattered the last winter spell. Every snowman in the county woke up wearing sunglasses.
lore.legendary: When the world forgot spring, Narcissara sounded one tiny golden note beneath the snow. The sun remembered the way home, and winter never forgave her.

names.legendary: Taraxion, Emperor of a Million Wishes

lore.common: Disguises itself as a perfectly respectable flower until the gardener brings out the shovel.
lore.uncommon: Opens a thousand tiny umbrellas whenever someone says Make a wish.
lore.rare: Grants wishes with technical accuracy. Ask for a new car and receive a toy one with excellent mileage.
lore.epic: Sent a blizzard of seeds through the town hall windows. By Monday, every council seat had a lawn growing through it.
lore.legendary: Each of Taraxion's drifting seeds carries an unspoken childhood wish. The wind scatters them across kingdoms, where the impossible sometimes takes root.

names.legendary: Palisadra, Keeper of Forbidden Gardens

lore.common: Keeps the football on the other side just long enough to ruin the game.
lore.uncommon: Moves its slats closer together whenever the neighbours start gossiping.
lore.rare: Grows an extra panel overnight to protect its favourite patch of dandelions.
lore.epic: Declared a border dispute between two gardens and conscripted every garden gnome. The ceasefire required a shared barbecue.
lore.legendary: Palisadra once fenced a king out of his own castle after he trampled the roses. The kingdom still celebrates the day the flowers won their independence.

names.legendary: Fernosaurus, Memory of the Green Age

lore.common: Unfurls its little green fist every morning and waves at the nearest snail.
lore.uncommon: Lives in the darkest corner of the garden. Describes full sunlight as offensive.
lore.rare: Can roll its frond across a footpath overnight. Joggers call the new carpet a hazard.
lore.epic: Spread across the archaeological dig and re-created an entire prehistoric forest before lunch. The scientists found the gift shop beneath a giant leaf.
lore.legendary: Long before flowers existed, Fernosaurus listened to dinosaurs argue beneath its leaves. It remembers exactly which chicken's ancestors were the worst behaved.

names.legendary: Ficus Maximus, Lord of Human Resources

lore.common: Drops one leaf every time someone moves its pot two centimetres.
lore.uncommon: Refuses to drink water unless the office blinds are arranged exactly right.
lore.rare: Leans towards every conversation about promotions. The manager has started holding meetings outside.
lore.epic: Shed its entire canopy during the board meeting and buried the directors in leaves. The minutes record a unanimous vote for gardening leave.
lore.legendary: When the corporation moved headquarters, Ficus Maximus refused to budge. Within a year the vines had reclaimed the old building and renamed it the Department of Photosynthesis.

names.legendary: Reelith, Who Pulled the Other Shore

lore.common: Clicks loudly enough to warn every fish in the lake that lunch has arrived.
lore.uncommon: Weaves its fishing line into knots too sophisticated for sailors to understand.
lore.rare: Reels in a canoe, a duck and its angler's hat before it catches dinner.
lore.epic: Caught a current beneath the lake and wound it into a spinning whirlpool. The swans demanded refunds for their very unexpected boat ride.
lore.legendary: Reelith once hooked the far bank and pulled until the lake was no wider than a garden pond. Its owner celebrated with tea; the fish began campaigning for more water.

names.legendary: Rodrigo, the Catcher of Impossible Fish

lore.common: Hooks the tree behind the angler every single time.
lore.uncommon: Brings home an old boot with the pride of a championship winner.
lore.rare: Catches fish that tell outrageous stories about bigger fish downstream. Believes every word.
lore.epic: Cast so far across the river that it stole a sausage off a barbecue. By sunset the villagers had declared fishing a competitive sport for dinner.
lore.legendary: Rodrigo once caught the reflection of the moon in a mountain lake and lifted it from the water like a silver fish. The real moon demanded it back before dawn.

names.legendary: Bouquetta, Queen of the Wandering Bees

lore.common: Drops half its petals between the flower shop and the front door.
lore.uncommon: Refuses to fit any vase without an extended argument about height.
lore.rare: Makes its recipient sneeze exactly when the romantic speech reaches its best line.
lore.epic: Launched itself over the wedding guests, caught the ceiling chandelier and showered everyone in rose petals. The bride demanded an encore.
lore.legendary: Bouquetta once called every bee in the kingdom to escort a lonely bouquet to its intended home. The delivery took three days, but the flowers arrived wearing golden crowns of honey.

names.legendary: Goalath, the Keeperless King

lore.common: Catches every football except the one somebody actually wants to score. The net says it has favourites.
lore.uncommon: Rings its posts like church bells whenever a striker misses. An entire neighbourhood now knows the team's scoring record.
lore.rare: Slides two inches left whenever a boastful striker lines up. Never cheats for anyone who says please.
lore.epic: Swallowed every penalty at the tournament until the referees had to climb inside and negotiate the release of the ball.
lore.legendary: Goalath guards a pitch that appears only during eclipses. No shot has ever passed its net, though nobody has seen a goalkeeper inside.

names.legendary: Floribella, Binder of the Two Kingdoms

lore.common: Wears a crown of flowers across the doorway. Drops a petal on guests it doesn't approve of.
lore.uncommon: Tangled itself round a birthday hat and refused to give it back.
lore.rare: Knows exactly when the guests will arrive and starts shedding petals five minutes before.
lore.epic: Draped itself across the high street and made every passerby part of an enormous flower parade. The buses joined in.
lore.legendary: When two kingdoms were at war, Floribella grew a chain of flowers between their capitals. Nobody could march across without stopping to smell the roses.

names.legendary: Gatelord Grendel, Warden of the Meadow

lore.common: Creaks open as though announcing a royal entrance. Usually it is just the neighbour's cat.
lore.uncommon: Won't close until someone has walked far enough away to be annoyed by it.
lore.rare: Opens for cows but slams shut on anyone carrying a picnic basket. Knows exactly who deserves a walk.
lore.epic: On market day the farm gate opened itself and led every animal to the town hall. The council spent three hours negotiating with a goat.
lore.legendary: Grendel has guarded the same meadow for five hundred years. No invading army has passed him, although every sheep knows the password.

names.legendary: Gazeboria, the Wandering Palace

lore.common: Shivers when the bunting moves and blames a breeze that nobody else can feel.
lore.uncommon: Announces a stiff breeze by making every napkin attempt an escape.
lore.rare: Catches the party balloons under its canopy and uses them as a crown.
lore.epic: Lifted off during the summer festival and landed on the village cricket pitch. The players used it for tea instead.
lore.legendary: Gazeboria appears in a different garden each full moon, hosting a feast for wandering spirits. Anyone who joins must bring a folding chair and a convincing story.

names.legendary: Geranima, the Red Queen of Windowsills

lore.common: Flaunts its lemon-scented leaves at every passing bee. The bees keep asking for the flowers instead.
lore.uncommon: Sulks when its pot is moved an inch. Has never forgiven the last window cleaner.
lore.rare: Its flowers flash bright red at night, fooling taxis into stopping by the front garden.
lore.epic: Spread through the entire town from one forgotten cutting. Every balcony became a red carpet and the mayor took credit.
lore.legendary: Geranima's ancient petals bloom even under snow. They say she once persuaded winter to take a holiday by filling its boots with summer flowers.

names.legendary: Verdantus, the Unmowable King

lore.common: Signs its name in bright green on every pair of clean trousers.
lore.uncommon: Tickles bare ankles until its victims perform a very undignified lawn dance.
lore.rare: Grows back taller every time the mower cuts it. The mower is beginning to suspect a personal grudge.
lore.epic: Swallowed a riding mower, a garden bench and the neighbour's shed during a single rainy weekend. The postman now carries a machete.
lore.legendary: Verdantus refused the first king's order to make a perfect lawn. His blades still grow through the palace marble, spelling out messages nobody dares translate.

names.legendary: Hibiscia, Painter of Summer Skies

lore.common: Opens one spectacular flower in the morning and drops it at tea time like a diva ending a performance.
lore.uncommon: Wears a bloom bigger than its own pot and insists the window faces the wrong way.
lore.rare: Changes the colours of nearby flowers to match its own bright petals. The gardener's rainbow bed is now entirely pink.
lore.epic: Bloomed across every balcony in the seaside town at once. The tourists thought the buildings were wearing enormous floral hats.
lore.legendary: Hibiscia grew from a seed washed ashore after the first summer storm. When she flowers, the greyest skies remember blue, and the sea turns the colour of her petals.

names.legendary: Pokewell, the Staff of Seven Peaks

lore.common: Clacks over rocks like a very persistent goat with a wooden leg.
lore.uncommon: Tests every puddle twice, just to be absolutely certain the hiker's boot gets wet.
lore.rare: Finds a safe stepping stone beneath rushing water when its owner can see nothing but foam.
lore.epic: Vaulted an entire hiking party across a mountain stream in one heroic bounce. The sheep on the far bank applauded by accident.
lore.legendary: Pokewell once tapped the ground atop seven peaks and woke the forgotten footpaths linking them. Travellers can still follow the faint marks when every modern map fails.

names.legendary: Hurdleheim, the Leap That Never Ends

lore.common: Trips the same runner twice and claims the second time was an accident.
lore.uncommon: Pops back upright just when the next runner thinks the lane is clear.
lore.rare: Grows a few inches with every approaching footstep. Officials now measure it with a ladder.
lore.epic: Gathered every hurdle on the track into a towering obstacle course overnight. The athletes entered the pole-vault instead.
lore.legendary: Hurdleheim guards a legendary finish line that only the bravest runners can cross. Those who clear it find that the next jump leads straight into their childhood playground.

names.legendary: Hortensia, the Colour-Sworn Queen

lore.common: Drinks every drop of water you give it and still asks for another jug.
lore.uncommon: Changes from pink to blue when the garden soil feels particularly dramatic.
lore.rare: Repaints its flowers overnight to match the colour of its neighbour's curtains.
lore.epic: Bloomed into a blue ocean of giant flowerheads across the town square. The seagulls spent a week trying to land on it.
lore.legendary: Hortensia guarded a garden where every flower could choose its own colour. When the kingdom fell, she gathered all its lost blues into her blossoms so no one would forget the sky.

names.legendary: Iridia, Daughter of the Seven Colours

lore.common: Opens its petals like a fancy invitation and refuses to explain the dress code.
lore.uncommon: Raises its sword-shaped leaves whenever a slug approaches the border.
lore.rare: Sees secret intentions through the eye-shaped patterns on its flowers. The frogs avoid its gaze.
lore.epic: Filled the royal garden with blooms that refracted the sunlight into a thousand rainbows. Every visiting knight put down their sword to stare.
lore.legendary: Iridia sprang from the first rainbow to touch a marsh after the great storms. Her flowers still hold seven colours the rain has never managed to wash away.

names.legendary: Hedera, the Wall That Would Not Fall

lore.common: Slithers into the gutter while everyone thinks it is being decorative.
lore.uncommon: Hugs the house so tightly that one morning the postman cannot find the door.
lore.rare: Shapes its leaves into a smiling face on the garden wall. The neighbours have begun smiling back.
lore.epic: Swallowed an entire mansion under a green blanket in one night. The estate agent now advertises it as a woodland retreat.
lore.legendary: Hedera held up a crumbling fortress after its last stones lost their strength. The castle's oldest guardians are now roots, and every spring its towers bloom.

names.legendary: Crassula, Keeper of the Emerald Fortune

lore.common: Drops one plump green leaf on the carpet and calls it a generous tip.
lore.uncommon: Grows a tiny baby plant whenever the gardener mentions money.
lore.rare: Produces coin-shaped leaves that turn into real copper pennies only when nobody is greedy enough to collect them.
lore.epic: Overran the windowsills of every bank in town and demanded interest in sunshine. The bankers learned to water their investments.
lore.legendary: Crassula guarded a merchant's last coin through a century of hardship. In spring it grew into a tree of jade leaves, each carrying the promise of a kinder bargain.

names.legendary: Jessamine, Mistress of Midnight Gardens

lore.common: Smells sweetest just after everyone has closed the bedroom window.
lore.uncommon: Climbs the trellis and leaves fragrant flowers in the neighbours' teacups.
lore.rare: Sends its perfume through locked doors, filling sleepers' dreams with impossible summer holidays.
lore.epic: Drew every moth in the county to one midnight garden. The street lights vanished behind fluttering silver wings.
lore.legendary: Jessamine keeps a secret garden that blooms only in the hours before dawn. Travellers follow its perfume to find a resting place when the road has forgotten their names.

names.legendary: Somniflor, Shepherd of Quiet Storms

lore.common: Invites every bee on the street over for lunch and refuses to set a table.
lore.uncommon: Makes the linen cupboard smell like a fancy spa, even when the towels are muddy.
lore.rare: One sniff settles the angriest dog into a contented heap of snoring fur.
lore.epic: Bloomed beside a noisy village fair and put the marching band, the carousel and the mayor to sleep. Only the bees finished their performance.
lore.legendary: Somniflor grows where thunder has forgotten how to roar. It soothed an ancient storm into gentle rain, and the valley's flowers still bloom to the rhythm of its sleeping breath.

names.legendary: Everleaf, the Last Green Promise

lore.common: Hitchhikes on a boot and enters the house with all the confidence of a paying guest.
lore.uncommon: Makes the loudest crunch in a forest whenever someone tries to walk quietly.
lore.rare: Waits until the gardener has swept the path, then drops right in the middle.
lore.epic: Summoned all the autumn leaves to bury the football pitch. The referee found the goalposts by following the muffled cheering.
lore.legendary: Everleaf clung to the oldest tree through a winter that froze the rivers solid. At spring's return, its single green vein awakened the first bud on every branch in the valley.

names.legendary: Lichoria, Memory of the First Rock

lore.common: Spreads little yellow freckles across the garden wall and calls it interior decorating.
lore.uncommon: Needs a hundred years to cross one boulder and insists it is making excellent time.
lore.rare: Grows a tiny map across a rock face. The paths lead to places the mountain used to be.
lore.epic: Covered the old mayor's statue in green-gold patterns overnight, transforming him into an ancient forest spirit. The town voted to keep the improvement.
lore.legendary: Lichoria clung to the first stone lifted from the sea when the world was young. Its slow, coloured patterns still record every storm that has passed across that stone's face.

names.legendary: Liliandra, Queen of the Perfumed Dawn

lore.common: Leaves orange pollen on the first white shirt that passes its vase.
lore.uncommon: Opens a blossom bigger than its own stem and expects applause.
lore.rare: Blooms with a tiny midnight pop that the household mistakes for a knock at the door.
lore.epic: Released a fragrant cloud over the royal garden party and turned every guest's white outfit a beautiful shade of golden orange. The dressmaker retired rich.
lore.legendary: Liliandra bloomed at sunrise in a valley that had forgotten the scent of spring. Her golden pollen crossed the hills on the morning breeze, and every sleeping garden opened its petals in answer.

names.legendary: Padmara, Crown of the Untroubled Waters

lore.common: Wakes in the mud looking far too immaculate for the company it keeps.
lore.uncommon: Rolls raindrops off its leaves like marbles and invites the frogs to play.
lore.rare: Opens a clean white bloom in the middle of the foulest swamp. Even the mosquitoes feel underdressed.
lore.epic: Rose through a flooded city overnight, lifting the stranded boats on an enormous bed of petals. Nobody could agree whether to thank it or paint it.
lore.legendary: Padmara sleeps beneath the deepest lake until the water remembers peace. When she blooms, even ancient storms stop for a moment to see their reflections.

names.legendary: Magnoloria, Herald of the First Bloom

lore.common: Drops a soft pink petal directly into every cup of tea below its branches.
lore.uncommon: Opens its flowers before the leaves arrive, then shivers dramatically at the last frost.
lore.rare: Blooms bright and proud on bare winter branches. The other trees have started accusing it of showing off.
lore.epic: Covered the city in such a thick blizzard of petals that the snowploughs returned to work wearing pink ribbons.
lore.legendary: Magnoloria bloomed on the last living branch after a hundred-year winter. The first petal fell, and from the place it touched, the spring began again.

names.legendary: Aceria, the Last Leaf of Autumn

lore.common: Rides the wind in tiny circles, then lands neatly in someone's tea.
lore.uncommon: Changes from green to fiery red just in time to upstage the flowers.
lore.rare: Spins across the orchard with a whisper of maple sweetness, luring squirrels after it.
lore.epic: Led a scarlet storm of fallen leaves through the city. Every statue emerged wearing a red crown, including the one of the mayor.
lore.legendary: Aceria was the last leaf to leave the first maple when winter came. She caught the season's final sunset in her veins, and now every autumn borrows its red from her.

names.legendary: Solmarra, the Bloom That Defied Night

lore.common: Turns its face toward the sun and complains whenever a cloud interrupts the conversation.
lore.uncommon: Smells just fierce enough to send the garden slugs packing for next door.
lore.rare: Glows through autumn fog, guiding lost bees back to the right flowerbed.
lore.epic: Grew a blazing orange wall around the vegetable patch, and the invading slugs formed a queue to surrender.
lore.legendary: Solmarra bloomed beneath a moonless sky and held the first light of morning inside her petals. Villagers still plant her descendants when the long nights arrive.

names.legendary: Aurelocator, Seeker of Sunken Crowns

lore.common: Goes wild over a rusty bottle cap and accepts no criticism about treasure quality.
lore.uncommon: Beeps at every belt buckle within three metres, embarrassing the beachgoers.
lore.rare: Detects coins buried beneath old paths by listening to their faint metallic dreams.
lore.epic: Convinced an entire seaside town to dig up the beach for buried gold. The treasure was a magnificent collection of ring pulls.
lore.legendary: Aurelocator found the last crown of a sunken kingdom deep beneath the tidal sands. It left the crown untouched, allowing the sea to keep its oldest secret.

names.legendary: Lady Coinbloom, Keeper of Wild Luck

lore.common: Braids its trunk every morning and looks offended when nobody compliments the hairstyle.
lore.uncommon: Grows a fresh leaf whenever someone opens a new shop. The shopkeeper gives it all the credit for the first sale.
lore.rare: Produces a golden leaf each time somebody declares that money cannot grow on trees. The leaves turn to confetti when grabbed.
lore.epic: Started shedding coins during the annual bank inspection. The bankers abandoned their ledgers and rushed outside with buckets.
lore.legendary: Lady Coinbloom grants fortunes only to those who plant her fallen seeds. Every greedy king who tried to uproot her found his treasury full of chocolate money by dawn.

names.legendary: Monstrosa, the House That Grew Leaves

lore.common: Grows dramatic holes in its leaves and blames an imaginary caterpillar.
lore.uncommon: Reaches for the window so insistently that the curtains have started moving out of the way.
lore.rare: Sends roots into furniture and refuses to return borrowed chairs.
lore.epic: Swallowed the living room under a canopy of enormous leaves. The family now needs a compass to find the television.
lore.legendary: Monstrosa grew from a single cutting in a forgotten palace. When the heirs returned, they found the throne room had become a rainforest and the king's crown was full of roots.

names.legendary: Mossmother, Keeper of Lost Footsteps

lore.common: Grows on the dampest step and smiles whenever a boot goes squelch.
lore.uncommon: Creeps across shady bricks so slowly that nobody notices until the whole path is soft.
lore.rare: Cushions a bare stone overnight. The forest animals have started booking seats.
lore.epic: Covered every pavement in the village with a green velvet carpet. The mayor declared it beautiful right before sliding into the duck pond.
lore.legendary: Mossmother has guarded the fallen trees of the oldest forest since before birds sang. Every footprint lost to time survives as a tiny hollow beneath her green cloak.

names.legendary: Oarion, the Ferryman's Last Hope

lore.common: Drenches the person sitting at the front of the rowing boat on every other stroke.
lore.uncommon: Makes the boat spin in a circle when its partner takes a break. Says it is sightseeing.
lore.rare: Rows against the current as if the river were merely a long treadmill.
lore.epic: Struck the water so fiercely that the boating lake split in two, revealing a perfectly dry path to the café. The ducks asked whether the bridge would be permanent.
lore.legendary: Oarion carried the last ferryman across a river no bridge could tame. With one silver stroke he calmed the waters, allowing a hundred lost families to cross before dawn.

names.legendary: Orchidessa, Empress of the Last Bloom

lore.common: Drops a flower every time someone moves its pot two centimetres.
lore.uncommon: Sends silver roots over the windowsill as though scouting for better accommodation.
lore.rare: Flowers the very morning its owner finally decides to throw it away.
lore.epic: Took over the conservatory with a network of aerial roots and declared the watering can its royal herald. The goldfish have requested asylum.
lore.legendary: Orchidessa bloomed only once each century, and each petal held the face of someone who had faithfully tended her. The last petal showed a very smug housecat.

names.legendary: Captain Whitewake of the Wild River

lore.common: Drips cold water down the paddler's sleeve with every innocent-looking stroke.
lore.uncommon: Switches sides so often the canoe travels in a very artistic zigzag.
lore.rare: Knows which current will carry a canoe safely between the rocks before the rapids even begin.
lore.epic: Turned a furious waterfall backwards with one impossible stroke. The fish looked profoundly insulted by the change in schedule.
lore.legendary: Captain Whitewake rowed a rescue canoe through a river of floating ice when every boat turned back. At dawn, all the stranded villages saw his paddle rise above the mist.

names.legendary: Lady Violara, the Winter Smiler

lore.common: Pulls an offended little face whenever someone waters the flower beside it first.
lore.uncommon: Blooms through frost just to make the sleepy daffodils look lazy.
lore.rare: Changes the expression on its petals to match the nearest person's secret mood.
lore.epic: Turned every flowerbed in the palace into a chorus of cheeky faces. The royal gardener resigned after the begonias started laughing.
lore.legendary: Lady Violara bloomed in the snow at the end of a hundred-year winter. Travellers followed her purple smile to the first patch of thawed earth and built a village around it.

names.legendary: Lady Conetta, Queen of Uninvited Parties

lore.common: Snaps its elastic against the chin just as the camera flashes.
lore.uncommon: Leans its point into the neighbour's ear throughout the birthday song.
lore.rare: Crowns whoever is nearest as the birthday hero, leaving the actual birthday child very annoyed.
lore.epic: Declared itself ruler of a surprise party and fired every party blower at the cake. The guests applauded until the icing arrived.
lore.legendary: Lady Conetta attended every coronation in the kingdom disguised as a humble paper cone. At the final ceremony, she crowned the royal jester and everyone agreed it was an improvement.

names.legendary: Lady Spathia of the Quiet Garden

lore.common: Collapses dramatically whenever the watering can is five minutes late.
lore.uncommon: Waves a white flower like a little flag each time the neighbours start arguing.
lore.rare: Absorbs a room's bad mood until its leaves stand upright again.
lore.epic: Stopped a furious office argument by drooping across the conference table. Nobody could continue shouting while fetching it water.
lore.legendary: Lady Spathia grew on the border of two kingdoms that had forgotten how to speak kindly. Her single white flower opened at dawn, and for the first time in a century, both armies laid down their banners.

names.legendary: Peonara, Heart of the Hidden Garden

lore.common: Invites ants to its buds and acts surprised when the petals are full of visitors.
lore.uncommon: Wears so many frilly petals that it needs a stick to stand upright after rain.
lore.rare: Opens overnight with a burst of perfume that makes even the grumpiest gardener smile at weeds.
lore.epic: Unfurled a flower the width of the village square. Its petals shaded a wedding, three market stalls and an extremely pleased cow.
lore.legendary: Peonara blooms once each century in a garden no map remembers. Whoever smells her first petal hears the name of the person who most needs their kindness.

names.legendary: Petunaria of the Endless Balcony

lore.common: Clings to your fingers after you touch a flower, like a very small handshake.
lore.uncommon: Spills purple blossoms from its basket and complains when anyone tidies them.
lore.rare: Grows across shop signs overnight, rewriting them with suspiciously cheerful floral slogans.
lore.epic: Trailed from every hanging basket in the city, transforming the entire high street into a fragrant maze. The taxis now navigate by colour.
lore.legendary: Petunaria once braided a thousand balcony flowers into a bridge for a lost child. Each summer it blooms again, though nobody can remember where the bridge first appeared.

names.legendary: Coniferra, Mother of a Thousand Pines

lore.common: Opens its scales on sunny days and shuts them when the rain arrives. It considers itself the weather forecast.
lore.uncommon: Gets chewed by a squirrel until it looks like a tiny wooden ice lolly.
lore.rare: Senses a coming storm and snaps its scales closed before the birds notice a cloud.
lore.epic: Launched a thousand winged seeds across a barren hillside during a gale. The hillside woke up green and the local goats are furious.
lore.legendary: Coniferra rolled from mountain to mountain on the winter winds, scattering seeds that became a forest joining two kingdoms. Every tree still points towards its wandering mother.

names.legendary: Papavera, Flower of the Unforgotten

lore.common: Opens its crinkled red petals and immediately loses one to the wind.
lore.uncommon: Shakes its little seed pod like a pepper pot whenever anyone walks past.
lore.rare: Blossoms on forgotten paths, drawing travellers back to places that deserve remembering.
lore.epic: Covered the scarred fields of a long-abandoned battlefield in a sea of red. The returning families finally found a quiet place to gather.
lore.legendary: Papavera blooms wherever the names of the lost are lovingly spoken. Its red petals carry their stories across the years, never demanding that sorrow be forgotten.

names.legendary: Pothoria, Green Veins of the Empty City

lore.common: Trails down from the shelf until its leaves tangle in the desk lamp.
lore.uncommon: Climbs the bookcase every night, searching for a more exciting book.
lore.rare: Wraps itself around the WiFi router, allowing only plant-care websites through.
lore.epic: Spread from one office plant across the entire building, tying every rolling chair to its desk. The employees voted to work in the garden.
lore.legendary: Pothoria crept through an abandoned city and wrapped its empty towers in green leaves. When the people finally returned, the old avenues had become living gardens.

names.legendary: Arundella of the Silent Wetland

lore.common: Tickles passing ducks with its slender leaves and pretends the wind did it.
lore.uncommon: Whistles the same three notes whenever the fishermen try to be quiet.
lore.rare: Can imitate the calls of every bird that has ever nested beside its pond.
lore.epic: Grew into a moving wall around the lake, shielding an entire village of frogs from a terrible drought.
lore.legendary: Arundella holds the voices of a vanished wetland in each hollow stem. When wind passes through her, every lost bird song returns for one evening.

names.legendary: Elastoria, the Emerald Canopy

lore.common: Collects dust on its shiny leaves and acts offended when anybody tries to clean them.
lore.uncommon: Leans so far toward the window that it starts reviewing the neighbours' curtains.
lore.rare: Springs a fallen object back into the air from a glossy leaf. The cat has requested a safety net.
lore.epic: Polished every leaf until the plant became a giant green mirror. The sunrise woke the town three hours early and demanded a refund.
lore.legendary: Elastoria grew one leaf polished enough to show tomorrow. Every breakfast the household consults it, while the cat tries to paw yesterday back into place.

names.legendary: Kaboomia, Mother of the Wandering Forest

lore.common: Bursts open when somebody brushes past and fires a dozen seeds into their socks.
lore.uncommon: Hitches a ride on a dog's fur and insists it has booked a holiday to the next street.
lore.rare: Rattles with hidden seeds like a tiny maraca, summoning the garden insects to dance.
lore.epic: Burst in the greenhouse with such force that seedlings sprouted in every flowerpot, watering can and gardener's boot.
lore.legendary: Kaboomia carries a sleeping forest inside a pod smaller than a thumb. Once every hundred springs she opens it into the wind, and a new woodland begins wherever the last seed falls.

names.legendary: Polarius, Staff of the Endless Ascent

lore.common: Drops its little snow basket in the first drift and acts offended when asked to retrieve it.
lore.uncommon: Taps the snow in perfect time with the ski instructor's very long lecture.
lore.rare: Pushes its skier across flat ground faster than the chairlift moves uphill.
lore.epic: Launched an entire ski team up the steepest slope using one magnificent double-pole push. The chairlift demanded redundancy pay.
lore.legendary: Polarius was the staff of the first mountain guide, planted at the summit through every storm. A skier who touches it can hear the safe route home in the rhythm of falling snow.

names.legendary: Sansevera, the Plant That Outwaited Time

lore.common: Stares sternly at the watering can and refuses a drink for another month.
lore.uncommon: Survives a forgotten corner so well that the other houseplants accuse it of cheating.
lore.rare: Guards the hallway with upright leaves that make intruders think they have entered a very green fortress.
lore.epic: Outlived three office relocations, two broken coffee machines and the entire management team. The pot is now listed as senior staff.
lore.legendary: Sansevera grew in the window of a palace that fell to dust around her. A thousand years later, her sword-shaped leaves still point toward the room where someone once promised to return.

names.legendary: Chlorophilia, Forest Matron

lore.common: Drops a baby plantlet into your tea and expects you to raise it.
lore.uncommon: Swings its offspring beneath the shelf like a botanical playground.
lore.rare: Sends dozens of hanging babies down the staircase to spy on visitors and steal their houseplant gossip.
lore.epic: Grew so many plantlets overnight that the entire apartment block became a hanging garden, with lifts replaced by vines.
lore.legendary: Chlorophilia once grew a green bridge from an empty windowsill to a distant island. Every leaf along the way bore a tiny root seeking home.

names.legendary: Nethelia, the Fair Divider

lore.common: Lets every important ball trickle over and acts surprised when the crowd groans.
lore.uncommon: Sags a little lower whenever the score becomes interesting.
lore.rare: Catches thunderous serves midair and returns them as dainty floating bubbles.
lore.epic: Stretched its woven body from one end of the city to the other, turning a friendly match into a two-hour commute.
lore.legendary: Nethelia drew the first line between rival champions with a thread of moonlit fibre. It has never chosen a side, even when kings begged.

names.legendary: Veldara, the Wandering Sanctuary

lore.common: Hides the last tent peg directly beneath the place you just sat down.
lore.uncommon: Jams its door zip at three in the morning and calls it enhanced security.
lore.rare: Keeps its campers dry while every surrounding tent floats away, then demands breakfast.
lore.epic: Unfolded into an enormous canvas city overnight, complete with streets, inns and a very confused campsite manager.
lore.legendary: Veldara sheltered an entire travelling people inside her stitched walls when no kingdom would grant them land. Her doorway still appears wherever a weary stranger needs rest.

names.legendary: Carduella, the Unbowed Crown

lore.common: Stabs the ankle of anyone who says this is a lovely shortcut.
lore.uncommon: Floats its fluffy seeds into freshly hung washing and calls it seed dispersal.
lore.rare: Catches every loose sock and scarf in a meadow, building a bizarre prickly wardrobe.
lore.epic: Raised a violet wall of thorns around the pasture so quickly that a herd of cows had to negotiate with the bees for entry.
lore.legendary: Carduella grew from the last unbroken thorn on an abandoned battlefield. Her purple flowers became a promise that even trampled earth could rise again.

names.legendary: Dionaea, Empress of the Hungry Garden

lore.common: Snaps shut on a raindrop, then sulks about its terrible lunch.
lore.uncommon: Waits absolutely still until a fly calls it a fake plant.
lore.rare: Catches mosquitoes so efficiently that the other windowsill plants send thank-you notes.
lore.epic: Grew jaws large enough to snap shut on the garden barbecue, then demanded the cook explain why the sausages weren't flying.
lore.legendary: Once guarded a secret garden by swallowing every thief's shadow. Visitors escaped unharmed, but their shadows spent years buzzing inside its crimson traps.

names.legendary: Virelia, the Stairway of Leaves

lore.common: Wraps one tendril round the garden gate and won't let visitors leave politely.
lore.uncommon: Borrows bicycles from the patio and returns them with flowers in the spokes.
lore.rare: Climbs a brick wall overnight, rearranging the windows into leafy portraits.
lore.epic: Wove every garden chair into a towering green sculpture. The family now eat dinner on the roof, where their table ended up.
lore.legendary: Grew from a single seed at the base of an abandoned tower. Its living staircase carried lost travellers back to sunlight, one green step at a time.

names.legendary: Viola Noctis, the Hidden Bloom

lore.common: Hides beneath a leaf whenever someone compliments its colour.
lore.uncommon: Gives off its sweetest scent only after you've walked away.
lore.rare: Turns an entire woodland path purple overnight without a single footprint.
lore.epic: Convinced every walker to tiptoe through its meadow. The deer began selling tiny slippers to tourists.
lore.legendary: Bloomed in the shadow of a fortress where no sunlight ever reached. Each petal held a fragment of dawn until the walls finally fell.

names.legendary: Netara, Guardian of the Last Rally

lore.common: Sags in the middle and blames the beach for moving.
lore.uncommon: Twangs in protest whenever a serve brushes the tape.
lore.rare: Shifts uphill with the tide, forcing both teams to play on dry land.
lore.epic: Sprang upward during the championship and caught every spike in one enormous web. The players had to negotiate the return of the ball.
lore.legendary: Stretched between two distant islands during a great summer tournament. Its final rally lasted until the moon rose, and the winning ball became a new star.

names.legendary: Elder Rambleroot, the Living Wayfinder

lore.common: Insists on tapping every puddle to see if it is secretly deep.
lore.uncommon: Points out so many interesting stones that a short walk takes four hours.
lore.rare: Taps a rhythm that helps tired walkers find their next step.
lore.epic: Planted itself in a field and grew into a twisting wooden walkway overnight. The hiking club walked to the summit before breakfast.
lore.legendary: Was carved from the root of a tree that remembered every road. Hold it gently and its grain points toward home, no matter how far the traveller has wandered.

names.legendary: Nymphaea, the Moon's Floating Garden

lore.common: Offers a frog a seat, then gently closes when it begins to snore.
lore.uncommon: Lets dragonflies land on its petals but charges mosquitoes rent.
lore.rare: Unfolds a bridge of round leaves across the deepest pond overnight.
lore.epic: Covered a lake in enormous green lily pads, turning the summer regatta into a very confused hopping contest.
lore.legendary: Blossomed in the first pond to reflect the moon. Every full moon its petals open into a floating garden where the oldest frogs gather to tell the water's stories.

names.legendary: Floramundi, the Unplanted Spring

lore.common: Grows cheerfully beside a road where nobody asked it to.
lore.uncommon: Throws petals at the bees and pretends it wasn't trying to start a party.
lore.rare: Spreads bright blossoms through the cracks of an abandoned car park.
lore.epic: Took over the city roundabout in one glorious explosion of colour. Commuters started taking the long way to work just to admire it.
lore.legendary: Returned life to a battlefield after the banners fell silent. Every spring new flowers bloom there without being planted, and no two blossoms ever wear the same colour.

names.legendary: Corona, the Circle of Returning

lore.common: Spins on its front-door hook until every visitor knocks on the wrong side.
lore.uncommon: Sheds pine needles into the shoes of anyone who forgets to say hello.
lore.rare: Knows which absent friend a doorway is waiting for and grows one new sprig when they return.
lore.epic: Lady Garlandgrave rolled through the winter festival, gathering every missing hat on her branches. She returned them in spring, decorated with bewildered robin nests.
lore.legendary: Corona has hung on the same village door through a hundred changing seasons. Whenever a traveller finally comes home, one of her berries turns gold, even if no one remains to open the door.
